title: Kingdom of Great Britain
capsule: The Kingdom of Great Britain was formed on 1 May 1707 when the Acts of Union merged the Kingdom of England (including Wales) and the Kingdom of Scotland under a single Parliament at Westminster, with Queen Anne as the first monarch. Under the Hanoverian succession beginning with George I in 1714, the kingdom expanded its first and second colonial empires, fought the Seven Years' War, lost the American colonies in 1783, and suppressed Jacobite risings in 1715 and 1745. The state was absorbed into the larger United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on 1 January 1801 by a further Act of Union with Ireland.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is well-defined by constitutional documents and parliamentary records; the geometric attestation beginning 1709 rather than 1707 likely reflects a minor dataset alignment issue rather than historical uncertainty.
